issues.description: Ingest accepts missing input directories and never clears results, so stale rows remain after files or rows are removed.
Ingest is not atomic across a run; per-row commits can leave a partially updated database after a later parser failure.
Harness B JSONL parsing assumes every decoded line is an object and crashes on arrays, strings, or numbers.
Harness B metrics are assumed to be a mapping, so non-object metrics can crash or produce misleading validation behavior.
Malformed Harness C XML raises an uncaught ParseError and aborts ingest instead of recording a warning.
Required identity fields like run_id, model, and task can be empty, allowing blank keys and accidental overwrites.
Harness A CSV headers are ignored, so reordered or malformed columns can silently corrupt parsed data.
Invalid JSON and invalid numeric scores are counted as missing_score, which hides distinct data-quality failures.
Reporting against a missing database silently creates an empty SQLite file, masking wrong --db paths.
CLI commands do not handle expected ingest/report errors, so users get raw tracebacks instead of actionable failures.
Fixture generation recursively deletes the target directory, making a mistaken path capable of wiping unrelated files.
Package metadata is minimal and lacks common distribution fields such as license, authors, and classifiers.
